doc.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Mingus tears up the piano over unpaid money
summary: At a gangster-owned club Mingus plucked out a piano's strings when unpaid, and the young players were terrified.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: plucks them out with his hands. And so Lonnie and I, we looked at that and here we are, we’ve auditioned to get in this man’s band, and we’re in his band now, and there he is over there tearing the piano up, three hundred pounds. We were like 20 years old, 19, 20. And it was like oh, man, we work for somebody like this. And these gangsters, this just shows you the power of psychosis. I don’t care who anybody is, if you act, if you seem to be more crazy, crazier than they are, it’s awesome. And everybody respects that. And they just didn’t do anything to the guy. They probably could have killed him. But he was actually more bizarre, more outrageous than they were, and so they were just awestruck. They did owe him the money. He tore the piano up and then cut out.

Well yeah I mean here’s a guy that doesn’t care anything about who you are or whether you’re supposed to be this tough guy and this, because I’m crazy. And crazy people are tough. And they are, they really are. I mean I’ve grappled with some in the middle of — and they are, they’re like ten men, and nobody did anything. And so Lonnie and myself, we were terrified at that time. And we went on and made the gig. I worked with Mingus for about 12 years off and on.
